players.product: ion-trap chip fabrication for Quantinuum (2026 Strategic Services and Supply Agreement)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Josh Jepsen (first earnings call after the spin-off from Honeywell completed on June 29, per CEO Jim Currier): Q2 sales increased 5% organically to $4.5 billion; adjusted EBIT was $1 billion, down 2% on unfavorable mix and an inventory obsolescence charge of approximately $50 million (excluding the charge adjusted EBIT would have grown 3%); adjusted EPS was $1.78, down on higher taxes and lower adjusted EBIT. Supply constraints shifted shipments to domestic defense and Engines & Power Systems OE, which have lower than group average margins; the obsolescence charge was mostly in Engines & Power Systems and is not expected to recur.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 sales $4.5 billion (+5% organic); adjusted EBIT $1 billion (-2%); adjusted EPS $1.78; approximately $50 million inventory obsolescence charge

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Josh Jepsen, Q2 by end market: commercial OE sales +6% led by double-digit growth in commercial air transport as customers' build rates rose; commercial aftermarket +8% with strength in air transport and business aviation (business aviation flight hours growing at a high single-digit rate; the Middle East conflict and higher fuel prices had no material impact on aftermarket demand); defense and space +3%, with U.S. sales up high single digit despite the wind-down of a long-term non-aero restricted defense program in Control Systems, offset by material shortages that cut international sales; international defense Q2 orders rose at a strong double-digit rate with a book-to-bill of 1.5. CEO Jim Currier: OE business is 50% commercial air transport and 50% business aviation; no shift of repair / spares demand away from Honeywell Aerospace seen.
quarterly_data.figure: commercial OE +6%; commercial aftermarket +8%; defense and space +3%; international defense book-to-bill 1.5

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jim Currier / CFO Josh Jepsen: orders over the past year increased 8% for a book-to-bill of 1.1, with all three end markets contributing and defense and space leading; year-to-date customer wins carry $15 billion of lifetime value, adding to more than $90 billion of commercial and defense platform content wins in the prior four years; the backlog grew with a little growth in past dues (CFO; CEO: a modest past due backlog increase), with past-due mix roughly in line with revenue mix (CEO, who said penalties for late delivery are possible but customers prioritise the supply investments).
quarterly_data.figure: orders +8% (past year), book-to-bill 1.1; $15 billion lifetime value of year-to-date wins; more than $90 billion of wins in the prior four years

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jim Currier: last month IndiGo, India's largest carrier, selected Honeywell Aerospace avionics and APUs for more than 800 future Airbus A320 family aircraft it has on order - the largest selectable equipment win in company history; in selectable equipment the company has won approximately 60% of the value of potential content on over 4,000 narrow-body aircraft in the last four years.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 800 Airbus A320 family aircraft; approximately 60% of potential selectable content on over 4,000 narrow-body aircraft (last four years)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jim Currier: Aeroméxico announced it will adopt Honeywell Aerospace's Surface Alert (SURF-A) runway-collision alert system across its entire Boeing 737 fleet of more than 100 aircraft; SURF-A is a software upgrade to existing Honeywell Aerospace equipment and the company continues to see strong momentum for it.

CEO Jim Currier / CFO Josh Jepsen: the supply base has not ramped as expected - year-over-year output growth rose from 3% in Q1 to 4% in Q2, with a lower ramp in June; the issue is contained to a handful of material and supplier bottlenecks in the mechanical supply base (CFO: castings, forgings, complex machining, bearings - 'much more unique to the mechanical side versus the electronic side'); critical and constrained suppliers are roughly 2% of a base of over 3,000 suppliers, and 98% are performing well. CEO: 'this is clearly a supply issue and not a demand issue'; the guide assumes Q3 and Q4 output growth similar to Q2, roughly 4%.
quarterly_data.figure: output growth 3% (Q1) to 4% (Q2); constrained / critical suppliers roughly 2% of over 3,000

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jim Currier: one constrained supplier's past due of roughly $15 million-$16 million unlocks hundreds of millions of dollars of revenue output for Honeywell Aerospace, an $18 billion revenue business - a small group of constrained suppliers has a disproportionate impact on output.
quarterly_data.figure: $15 million-$16 million past due at one supplier; $18 billion revenue business

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jim Currier / CFO Josh Jepsen, supply actions: new sources added for over 50 constrained parts in H1 2026 with another 50 planned in H2, increasing multi-source components by 15% this year; resources embedded at critical suppliers led to a 20% quarter-over-quarter output increase at one key supplier; four times larger investment in multi-sourcing and in-sourcing this year than last; supplier tooling purchases doubling between 2025 and 2027, 70% of tooling spend going to constrained castings; over $1 billion invested in recent years; schedule attainment percentages doubled year over year and repair and overhaul turnaround times fell materially.
quarterly_data.figure: over 50 parts new-sourced in H1 + 50 planned in H2; multi-source components +15% in 2026; 20% output increase at one key supplier; 70% of supplier tooling to castings; over $1 billion invested in recent years

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Josh Jepsen, revised 2026 outlook (set to be achievable without dramatic supply chain improvement): organic sales growth of 4%-5%; pro forma standalone adjusted EBIT of $4.35 billion-$4.45 billion; new pro forma standalone EPS guidance of $7.60-$7.90; second-half free cash flow unchanged at $1 billion-$1.5 billion; capital expenditures of approximately $650 million. By end market: commercial OE mid-single-digit growth, commercial aftermarket low-to-mid-single-digit, defense and space mid-single-digit with domestic outpacing international.
quarterly_data.figure: organic sales +4%-5%; adjusted EBIT $4.35 billion-$4.45 billion; EPS $7.60-$7.90; H2 free cash flow $1 billion-$1.5 billion; capex approximately $650 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Josh Jepsen: versus the Investor Day guide, sales growth is down 3%-4% at the midpoint (mostly lower mechanical supply and mix, some lower international defense output) and EBIT is down about $300 million at the midpoint ($50 million inventory obsolescence plus a mix shift from aftermarket to OE and from international to domestic defense); Q3 expected flat to up slightly year over year (toughest comp: Q3 2025 commercial aftermarket was up 23%), Q4 up in line with the full-year guide; pro forma standalone 2025 free cash flow was $2.5 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: sales growth guide down 3%-4% at midpoint; EBIT guide down about $300 million at midpoint; 2025 pro forma free cash flow $2.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jim Currier: reiterating the 2030 targets and expecting accelerating sales and profit growth in 2027 as supply constraints resolve, driven by supply-base and capacity investments, incremental missiles and munitions sales from the framework agreement with the Department of Defense, repricing of long-term agreements to recoup cost inflation of the past five to 10 years (materialising in 2027 and beyond), RMU upgrades such as radio altimeters meeting the FAA's 5G-tolerance mandate, and the not-supply-limited 2024 acquisitions CAES and Civitanavi. CFO: second-half growth of about 12% last year combined with this year's second-half outlook gives a normalized CAGR of about 7%-8% for the last two years, in line with the long-term framework.

CEO Jim Currier, capacity: a new production line in Arizona delivered initial operational test units for Assure, the advanced electromechanical actuation system; expansion progressing at the Minnesota facility for critical inertial sensing components for navigation systems; 70% of capital investments are external (suppliers) and 30% internal capacity. Anthem next-generation avionics advanced formal qualification on major subsystems in Q2; R&D spending is roughly 10% of sales, the majority customer-funded.
quarterly_data.figure: 70% external / 30% internal capital investment; R&D roughly 10% of sales

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jim Currier: international defense is approximately 30% of the defense and space end market, with high single-digit annual growth anticipated through 2030; the acquisition of Civitanavi (Italy; navigation solutions including the ARGO 4000 inertial measurement unit for missiles, unmanned platforms, vessels and land vehicles in GPS-denied conditions) expands the European manufacturing footprint, and Civitanavi sales are expected to double in 2026 versus the prior year.
quarterly_data.figure: international defense approximately 30% of defense and space; Civitanavi sales expected to double in 2026
